title: Clear the station codes
prompt: The weather dashboard plots every reading, and the stations' -9999 code for "no value" wrecks its charts. Write `solve(observations)` so it returns every reading with that code turned into an empty value (null) in `temperature_c`, `humidity_pct`, `wind_speed_kph` and `pressure_hpa`.
rules: Keep every row and every column, in the same order, with the same types.
Only -9999 changes. Every other value stays as it is, including other negative numbers.
A reading with -9999 in several of the four columns gets null in each of them.
Leave NaN in `precipitation_mm` alone: gauge faults are reported separately.
hints: Nothing is removed here, so this isn't a `filter` or a `dropna`: you replace values and keep the rows.
`df.na.replace(old, new, subset=[...])` swaps one value for another in the columns you list, and `new` can be `None`.
Replacing -9999 with `None` in the four columns gives nulls without changing any column's type. Replacing with 0 would invent readings.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(observations):
    # Return every reading with the -9999 code turned into null.
    return observations
explanation: This is a replacement, not a filter: every reading stays, only the code changes. `observations.na.replace(-9999, None, subset=["temperature_c", "humidity_pct", "wind_speed_kph", "pressure_hpa"])` swaps -9999 for null in those four columns and keeps every type, including the whole-number `humidity_pct`. NaN in `precipitation_mm` isn't -9999, so it stays. A `select` with `F.when(F.col(c) == -9999, None).otherwise(F.col(c))` for each of the four columns gives the same result but is much longer. Replacing with 0 instead of `None` would turn a missing reading into a real-looking one, and `dropna` or a `filter` would throw away readings the dashboard still needs.
